author: IGN
description: We just got our second trailer for the upcoming live-action Resident Evil movie from Weapons and Barbarian director Zack Cregger. There's been a lot of discussion about whether or not this movie will do the source material justice, but the new trailer definitely sells the idea a lot better than the last one: this is a movie based on what it's like to play Resident Evil, but set in the Resident Evil universe. Finding new weapons, scrounging for ammo and supplies, and frantically trying to avoid enemies are all crucial parts of the survival horror experience, and this trailer gives us glimpses of all that without spoiling what happens in the movie. After all, the fun part of a horror movie is not knowing what's lurking behind every corner. Leon Kennedy probably isn't going to show up, but will show us new corners of Raccoon City, new creatures hiding there, and will probably feature a few easter eggs along the way. And hey, ya know what? If it sucks, at least we have Resident Evil Veron

author: IGN
description:
Halo: Campaign Evolved reviewed by Michael Higham on PC, also available on Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5.

It's no secret that Halo: Campaign Evolved is a test run for developer Halo Studios and its future using the Unreal Engine, and from that perspective, it makes sense why this is a pretty slim package that retreads well-worn territory. The fact that I still had a blast revisiting the original Halo story in 2026 speaks to its timelessness, however, and the gunplay that revolutionized first-person console games and co-op multiplayer make it worth playing today. But that's largely a credit to Halo in general, and not necessarily Campaign Evolved, specifically. The new prequel missions are a fun couple of hours of usual Halo fare, and the elevation in technical detail with UE5 and the subtle tweaks in the older missions are nice to see. But I don't think they're transformative in a way that makes a significant difference to what's been great about Halo even two-something decades l
title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Review

author: IGN
description:
The remake of the original Halo game Combat Evolved is here. Halo: Campaign Evolved is a total remake from the ground up of the genre defining shooter that not only has completely overhauled visuals and modern gameplay elements, but for the first time ever, a main line Halo game is playable on a PlayStation. 

The game looks incredible on both PlayStation 5 pro, and Xbox Series X and on both platforms you have two graphics modes to choose from, Performance and Quality. 

On Series X in quality mode you get the game running at a stable 30fps with better visuals and a dynamic 4k output while Performance mode offers dynamic scaling at a buttery smooth targeted 60fps.

On PlayStation 5 pro you pretty much get the same options. Quality is upscaled via PSSR with a target frame rate of 30fps while performance hits 60fps. Load times were faster on PS5 Pro, but that’s hardly saying much since the load times were pretty quick on Xbox to begin with.  
Regardless of where you play Campaign evolve
title: Halo: Campaign Evolved - PlayStation 5 Pro vs Xbox Series X Graphics Comparison
